source_evidence.text: I founded a twenty-six-person architecture practice thirty years ago and want to step back within two years.
A regional engineering group has offered to buy the firm, keep the name for five years, and give me a clean financial exit.
Several senior architects have also asked whether I would consider selling the firm to employees instead.
I want the practice to outlast me, but I am attracted to the certainty of the external offer and worried that an internal transition could consume my final working years.
I cannot tell how much of my preference for employee ownership is about protecting the firm's culture and how much is about wanting my colleagues to validate what I built.
